questions.question: Two elements X and Y have 2 and 7 valence electrons respectively and they have same number of electron shells. Their electron affinities are:
questions.solution: (b) X < Y. In the same period, electron affinity increases from left to right; Y (7 valence electrons) readily gains one electron to complete its octet.

questions.question: The cation which gets reduced first during the electrolysis of a solution which contains Cu2+, Ag1+ and H1+ of the same concentration.
questions.solution: (b) Ag1+. Silver is lowest in the electrochemical series, so Ag+ ions are discharged (reduced) first: Ag+ > Cu2+ > H+.

questions.question: P, Q, R and S are the elements with atomic numbers 6, 11, 16 and 8 respectively. The formula of the compound between Q and S:
questions.solution: (b) Q2S. Q is sodium (2,8,1, valency 1) and S is oxygen (2,6, valency 2), so the compound is Na2O, i.e. Q2S.

questions.question: A molecule of .......... contains three covalent bonds.
questions.solution: (c) Ammonia. NH3 has three N-H single covalent bonds. (N2 has one triple bond, which is also three shared pairs, but it is counted as a triple bond between two atoms; the expected answer is ammonia.)

questions.question: The gas which turns Starch iodide paper blue black:
questions.solution: (b) Cl2. Chlorine displaces iodine from KI; the liberated iodine turns starch blue-black.

concepts: molecular formula = n x empirical formula
questions.question: The molecular weight of a compound is 90. The empirical formula weight is 30. Then:
questions.solution: (c) n = 3. n = molecular weight / empirical formula weight = 90 / 30 = 3.

questions.question: The basic gas produced when solid ammonium chloride undergoes thermal decomposition:
questions.solution: (d) NH3. NH4Cl -> NH3 + HCl on heating; ammonia is the basic gas.

questions.topic: Reactivity of metals down a group
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The tendency of losing electrons increases down the group.
Reason (R): The most reactive metal is placed at the top of Group I.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

questions.solution: (c) A is true but R is false. Atomic size increases down a group, so electrons are lost more easily; the most reactive metal is therefore at the bottom of Group I.

questions.question: An unsaturated hydrocarbon used for welding purposes.
questions.solution: (c) Acetylene. Ethyne burns in oxygen with a very hot oxy-acetylene flame used for welding and cutting metals.

questions.question: The number of moles present in 10 g of CaCO3. [At. wt of Ca = 40; C = 12; O = 16]
questions.solution: (b) 0.1 mole. Molar mass CaCO3 = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g; 10/100 = 0.1 mol.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Froth floatation is a method of concentration of sulphide ores.
Reason (R): In this method the ore is wetted by water and the impurities are wetted by the oil.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

questions.solution: (c) A is true but R is false. In froth floatation the sulphide ore particles are preferentially wetted by the oil and rise with the froth, while the gangue is wetted by water and sinks.

questions.question: The electrode reaction at cathode during the electroplating of an article with silver metal using silver salt is:
questions.solution: (b) Ag1+ + 1e- -> Ag. Reduction occurs at the cathode where silver ions gain electrons and deposit on the article.

questions.question: The formula which represents saturated hydrocarbon is.
questions.solution: (b) C5H12. Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) have the general formula CnH2n+2; n = 5 gives C5H12.

questions.question: The main metal present in the alloy Solder is:
questions.solution: (d) Lead. Solder is an alloy of lead and tin (typically Pb 50%, Sn 50%), with lead as the main metal as per the ICSE syllabus.

questions.question: The gas that decolourises Potassium permanganate (KMnO4) solution is:
questions.solution: (a) Sulphur dioxide. SO2 is a reducing agent and decolourises acidified pink/purple KMnO4.

questions.question:
The following questions are pertaining to the laboratory preparation of Hydrogen chloride gas.
[Diagram: NaCl in a round-bottom flask heated on a tripod, with H2SO4 added through a thistle funnel; the gas passes through a bottle containing substance A and emerges as 'dry gas', which is collected in a gas jar B.]
(a) Give the role of substance 'A'.
(b) Write balanced equation for the reaction that takes place in the round bottom flask.
(c) Why is the temperature of the reaction mixture kept below 200 C?
(d) State the method of collection of the gas.
(e) How will you identify the gas after collection?
questions.solution:
(a) A is concentrated sulphuric acid; it acts as a drying agent and removes moisture from the HCl gas.
(b) NaCl + H2SO4 (conc) --(below 200 C)--> NaHSO4 + HCl
(c) Above 200 C, sodium sulphate is formed which forms a hard crust sticking to the flask that is difficult to remove and may crack the flask; it also wastes fuel. Below 200 C the reaction stops at NaHSO4.
(d) Upward displacement of air (HCl is heavier than air, vapour density 18.25 vs 14.4).
(e) Bring a glass rod dipped in ammonia solution near the mouth of the jar: dense white fumes of ammonium chloride are formed (NH3 + HCl -> NH4Cl). (Also turns moist blue litmus red.)

marking_points.point: (c) Avoid Na2SO4 crust / flask cracking / fuel waste
(e) Dense white fumes with ammonia rod

questions.figure_desc: Laboratory preparation of HCl: NaCl and H2SO4 heated in round-bottom flask, gas through drying bottle A, dry gas collected in gas jar B.

questions.topic: Catalysts and conditions of industrial processes
questions.question:
Match the following columns:
Column I: (a) Contact Process (b) Esterification (c) Hydrogenation (d) Ostwald's Process (e) Haber's Process
Column II: (i) Platinum (ii) Iron (iii) Vanadium Pentoxide (iv) Nickel (v) Conc. H2SO4
questions.solution:
(a) Contact process - (iii) Vanadium pentoxide
(b) Esterification - (v) Conc. H2SO4
(c) Hydrogenation - (iv) Nickel
(d) Ostwald's process - (i) Platinum
(e) Haber's process - (ii) Iron

questions.question:
Choose the correct answer from the brackets:
(a) The gas produced on the action of dil. HCl on metal sulphite is ........ (SO2 / SO3)
(b) ........ (Silver / Copper) compounds are easily reduced to corresponding metal by heating alone.
(c) The molecule which has two lone pair of electrons is ........ (NH3 / H2O).
(d) Dilute HCl and dilute H2SO4 can be distinguished by adding ........ (NaNO3 / BaCl2) solution.
(e) Substitution reactions are characteristic reactions of ........ (alkenes / alkanes).

answer_items.prompt: Gas from dil. HCl on metal sulphite
Reagent distinguishing dil. HCl and dil. H2SO4

questions.solution:
(a) SO2 (Na2SO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + SO2)
(b) Silver (compounds of less reactive metals such as Ag and Hg are reduced by heat alone)
(c) H2O
(d) BaCl2 (gives white ppt of BaSO4 with dil. H2SO4, none with dil. HCl)
(e) Alkanes

questions.question:
Identify the following:
(a) The process of crushing the ore into fine powder.
(b) The energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous isolated atom to form a negatively charged ion.
(c) The tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms.
(d) The process by which certain ores, specially carbonates, are converted to oxides by heating in the absence of air.
(e) A type of covalent bond in which electrons are shared equally between the combining atoms.

answer_items.prompt: Crushing the ore into fine powder
Energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom
Tendency to form chains of identical atoms
Converting carbonate ores to oxides by heating in absence of air

questions.solution:
(a) Pulverisation
(b) Electron affinity
(c) Catenation
(d) Calcination
(e) Non-polar covalent bond

questions.question:
Draw the structural diagram of the following organic compounds:
(i) 2-methyl propan-1-ol
(ii) Acetic acid
(iii) 2, 3 - dimethyl butane
questions.solution:
(i) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol: (CH3)2CH-CH2-OH; a three-carbon chain with -OH on C-1 and a -CH3 branch on C-2, all bonds shown.
(ii) Acetic acid (ethanoic acid): CH3-COOH, i.e. H3C-C(=O)-O-H with all bonds shown.
(iii) 2,3-Dimethylbutane: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(CH3)-CH3; a four-carbon chain with one -CH3 branch on C-2 and one on C-3, all bonds shown.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Calculate:
(a) The percentage composition of phosphorous in the fertilizer super phosphate Ca(H2PO4)2. [At. wt: H = 1; P = 31; O = 16; Ca = 40]
(b) The Molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH2O and its vapour density is 30. [At. wt: H = 1; C = 12; O = 16]
questions.solution:
(a) Molar mass of Ca(H2PO4)2 = 40 + 2(2 x 1 + 31 + 4 x 16) = 40 + 2(97) = 234 g.
Mass of P = 2 x 31 = 62 g.
% P = (62 / 234) x 100 = 26.5%.
(b) Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 2 x 30 = 60.
Empirical formula mass of CH2O = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30.
n = 60 / 30 = 2, so molecular formula = (CH2O)2 = C2H4O2.

marking_points.point: (b) Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 60; EF mass = 30

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Differentiate between the following pairs using the criteria given:
(a) Carbonic acid and Acetic acid (Type of salts formed)
(b) Weak electrolyte and Non-electrolyte (Kind of particles present)
questions.solution:
(a) Carbonic acid is dibasic and forms two types of salts: acid salts (e.g. NaHCO3) and normal salts (e.g. Na2CO3). Acetic acid is monobasic and forms only normal salts (e.g. CH3COONa).
(b) A weak electrolyte contains both ions and (mostly) un-ionised molecules; a non-electrolyte contains only molecules (no ions).

marking_points.point: (a) Carbonic acid: acid + normal salts; acetic acid: only normal salt
(b) Weak electrolyte: ions and molecules; non-electrolyte: only molecules

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Rohit was trying to electroplate an iron cup with Nickel metal. He has some doubts regarding the electroplating. Help Rohit by answering the following questions:
[Diagram: electrolytic cell with a battery and ammeter; a thick rod is the anode and the iron cup hangs as the cathode, both dipped in the electrolyte.]
(a) Why the iron cup is placed at the cathode?
(b) What happens to the anode after sometime?
(c) State one condition that is necessary to ensure that the deposit is smooth, firm and even.
questions.solution:
(a) Nickel ions (Ni2+) are positive and migrate to the cathode, where they gain electrons and are deposited as nickel metal; so the article to be plated is made the cathode.
(b) The nickel anode gradually becomes thinner (dissolves) as Ni atoms lose electrons and go into solution as Ni2+ ions.
(c) A low current for a longer time (or low concentration of the electrolyte / the article kept rotating / clean article).

marking_points.point: (a) Ni2+ ions are reduced and deposited at the cathode
(b) Anode becomes thinner / dissolves as Ni2+
(c) Low current for longer time (or equivalent)

questions.question:
Draw the Electron dot (cross dot) structures of the following:
(a) Hydronium ion (b) Calcium Oxide
questions.solution:
(a) Hydronium ion: the O atom of water (two shared pairs with two H atoms, two lone pairs) donates one lone pair to H+ forming a coordinate bond; [H3O]+ shows three bonding pairs around O and one lone pair, overall charge +1.
(b) Calcium oxide: Ca (2,8,8,2) transfers two electrons to O (2,6), giving [Ca]2+ and [O]2- (with 8 electrons around O); ionic bond.

marking_points.point: (a) H3O+ with coordinate bond and one lone pair on O, + charge
(b) Ca2+ and O2- formed by transfer of two electrons

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give reasons for the following:
(a) Electrolysis of molten lead bromide is considered a redox reaction.
(b) Ethane undergoes substitution reaction while ethene undergoes addition reaction.
questions.solution:
(a) At the cathode Pb2+ ions gain electrons (reduction: Pb2+ + 2e- -> Pb) and at the anode Br- ions lose electrons (oxidation: Br- - e- -> Br; 2Br -> Br2); both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
(b) Ethane is saturated (only C-C single bonds) so its H atoms can only be replaced; ethene is unsaturated with a C=C double bond, so atoms add across the double bond.

marking_points.point: (a) Reduction at cathode and oxidation at anode together
(b) Ethane saturated (single bonds); ethene unsaturated (double bond)

questions.question:
Hydrochloric acid is prepared by dissolving hydrogen chloride in water as per the arrangement given below:
[Diagram: HCl gas led through a tube into an inverted funnel whose rim just touches the water in a trough; when water rises into the funnel an air gap forms and the water level outside falls.]
(a) What is the above arrangement called as?
(b) What precaution needs to be taken during the above method of preparation of hydrochloric acid?

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Name the method used for the preparation of the following salts from the list given below.
Simple displacement - P
Neutralisation - Q
Neutralisation-Titration - R
Precipitation - S
(a) Ammonium sulphate
(b) Lead carbonate
(c) Copper (II) chloride
questions.solution:
(a) R - Neutralisation by titration (2NH4OH + H2SO4 -> (NH4)2SO4 + 2H2O; both reactants are soluble)
(b) S - Precipitation (Pb(NO3)2 + Na2CO3 -> PbCO3 + 2NaNO3; insoluble salt)
(c) Q - Neutralisation (CuO + 2HCl -> CuCl2 + H2O; insoluble base with acid)
